events_seen: TRADE (Jul 19): Corbishley receives Michael Wilson (WR, ARI), Tee Higgins (WR, CIN), Breece Hall (RB, NYJ), 2027 R2 pick. Fronge receives TreVeyon Henderson (RB, NE), Kyle Monangai (RB, CHI), Nico Collins (WR, HOU), 2028 R2 pick.
TRADE (Jul 17): Adam receives Justin Herbert (QB, LAC). Fronge receives Jacory Croskey-Merritt (RB, WAS), C.J. Stroud (QB, HOU), 2028 R1 pick.
TRADE (Jul 10): Adam receives Keaton Mitchell (RB, LAC). Wingard receives 2028 R3 pick.
WAIVER CLAIM (Jun 21): Drew added Colbie Young (WR, CIN) (dropped Joe Mixon (RB, FA)).
WAIVER CLAIM (Jun 08): Adam added Cyrus Allen (WR, KC) (dropped Phil Mafah (RB, DAL)).
WAIVER CLAIM (May 27): Charles added Chris Brooks (RB, GB) for $1 FAAB (dropped Austin Ekeler (RB, FA)).
WAIVER CLAIM (May 16): Charles added Matt Hibner (TE, BAL) (dropped Moliki Matavao (TE, NO)).
CUT (May 16): Charles released Zonovan Knight (RB, ARI).
WAIVER CLAIM (May 13): Shaq added Zavion Thomas (WR, CHI).
WAIVER CLAIM (May 12): Adam added John Michael Gyllenborg (TE, KC) (dropped Elijah Higgins (TE, ARI)).

tweets.name: Dina Ravioli
tweets.text: The Deepwater asset I've been tracking — I can now confirm there's a formal offer on the table. The player is a wideout. The return involves future capital. Filing when terms clear but Mitchum has a decision to make and the clock is not theoretical anymore.

tweets.name: Bo Ruckman
tweets.text: Dina just said 'the clock is not theoretical' and I need SOMEONE to give me a segment on this because I have been saying Deepwater is a live situation since before it was fashionable to say that and now suddenly everyone's an analyst.

tweets.name: Matteo Honeydew
tweets.text: Ranking the Corbishley-Fronge trade a week out: Apex got better at wideout, unambiguously. Tee Higgins on a roster built for volume is the kind of asset that looks obvious in hindsight. Breece Hall is the interesting one — Apex needed RB depth and got RB depth with upside, which is a different thing. Fronge got younger and cheaper. Whether that's wisdom or necessity is the real question.

tweets.name: Terrence E. Odom
tweets.text: Nico Collins to ForgeHammer in that deal. A receiver of that caliber, in a Havana-based operation with zero pick liquidity and a head coach who relocated for 'regulatory flexibility.' I am not saying it cannot work. I am saying the conditions required for it to work are extraordinarily specific and Fronge has not yet demonstrated he can engineer them.

tweets.name: Vance Hollis
tweets.text: Herbert confirmed at Helix, Stroud goes to ForgeHammer, and the market is somehow sleeping on the fact that Adam just solved the one thing that was keeping HLX from being a genuine title contender in a superflex format. That +34.9% preseason bump was the appetizer.

tweets.name: Chad Bellwether
tweets.text: Everyone treating the ForgeHammer Havana relocation as a distraction is missing the point entirely. Geographical distance from the other eleven GMs is a proven cognitive advantage. I have been saying this about corner offices for years. Fronge is simply applying it at scale.

tweets.name: Jay Kelpey
tweets.text: The Corbishley trade gets all the attention but nobody's talking about what ForgeHammer's depth chart looks like at RB now. Henderson and Monangai are both good. Neither is a locked-in bell cow. In a 0.5 PPR format you need to know whose touches are real and whose are committee scraps. That's not settled.

tweets.name: Marty Volkman
tweets.text: Hearing rumblings — and I want to be clear these are rumblings, not a report, not a scoop, more of an atmospheric pressure change — that at least one team currently described as 'quiet this offseason' is not planning to remain quiet. Per two people who used the word 'quiet' to me.

tweets.name: Vivienne Ashcroft
tweets.text: Tonight on the Exchange Report: Dina has new detail on Deepwater, Vance wants to reprice every QB1 in the league following the Herbert move, and Terrence has prepared what he called — unprompted, before I finished asking — 'a full verdict on Fronge's decision-making framework.' That is either twelve minutes of television or four. Nine o'clock.
